claims.headline: Reported Central London availability down 20% year on year
claims.text: Semafor reported on 9 October 2026 that Canary Wharf Group's latest earnings showed availability in Central London fell 20% year on year, while supply in Docklands stayed broadly steady. No reference period or measurement definition is given.

claims.headline: Canary Wharf Group reports record rents and 92%+ occupancy
claims.text: The same 9 October 2026 report states Canary Wharf Group is reporting the highest rental rates in its history and that office occupancy there now exceeds 92%. These are company-scope figures, not a Central London market rent or occupancy measure.

claims.headline: Large Canary Wharf occupier commitments reported
claims.text: Semafor reported on 9 October 2026 that Visa recently leased 300,000 sq ft, Barclays bought its headquarters for £750 million, and Citi is investing more than $1 billion in its European HQ; JPMorgan has proposed a £3 billion, 265-metre tower subject to approval.

claims.headline: Canary Wharf refurbishment marketed to defence and AI occupiers
claims.text: Reuters-sourced reporting published 5 October 2026 says developer LS Estates is sounding out defence and AI companies for a refurbished nine-floor Canary Wharf office formerly occupied by Credit Suisse support staff. This is marketing interest, not a signed letting.

claims.headline: Life-science lab demand at 17 Columbus Courtyard below expectations
claims.text: The same 5 October 2026 report says the £100 million-plus refit of 17 Columbus Courtyard, backed by GIC and Oaktree, had earmarked up to 60% of space for laboratories but life-sciences interest was lower than expected in the short term.

claims.headline: Lambeth HQ refurbishment planning permission granted
claims.text: London Fire Brigade announced on 6 October 2026 that it received planning permission from Lambeth Council to refurbish its historic Albert Embankment headquarters to provide a fire station, office space and community spaces. Permission is not completed refurbishment or occupation.

claims.headline: Knight Frank: development lagging occupier demand
claims.text: Knight Frank commentary published 7 October 2026 argues London office development activity is not keeping pace with occupier demand for the type of space now required, attributing this partly to viability pressures and partly to macroeconomic caution weighing on investors.

claims.headline: Landlord view: majority of occupiers expanding footprint
claims.text: Canary Wharf Group's chief executive told Semafor (9 October 2026) that roughly 60% of its office occupiers grew footprint over the last 18 months, 20% were flat and 20% shrank, and that tenants increasingly agree they need the best space to compete for talent.

claims.headline: Source forecast: London supply shortage to worsen next year
claims.text: The same 9 October 2026 report attributes to Canary Wharf Group's chief executive a forecast that the shortage of supply elsewhere in London will worsen next year, which he links to UK regulations raising construction costs and deterring new development.

claims.headline: Central London Q2 2026 take-up 2.4m sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported Central London take-up of 2.4 million sq ft across 192 transactions in Q2 2026 (reference period 1 April to 30 June 2026), published 6 August 2026.

claims.headline: Central London take-up up 0.2m sq ft quarter on quarter
claims.text: Deterministic comparison of Savills Central London take-up shows Q2 2026 at 2.4 million sq ft versus 2.2 million sq ft in Q1 2026, a rise of 0.2 million sq ft (9.1%). This is a quarterly change, not a weekly movement.

claims.headline: Central London vacancy 7.2%, City unchanged at 7.0%
claims.text: Savills reported the Central London vacancy rate declined 20 basis points to 7.2% in Q2 2026, and the City vacancy rate remained unchanged at 7.0%. Savills vacancy is not availability.

claims.headline: Central London vacancy down 0.2pp quarter on quarter
claims.text: Deterministic comparison of Savills Central London vacancy shows 7.2% in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% in Q1 2026, a fall of 0.2 percentage points (2.7% relative). Quarterly, not weekly.

claims.headline: Reported Central London supply down 0.4m sq ft in Q2
claims.text: Savills reported Central London office supply of 18.7 million sq ft at end-Q2 2026 versus 19.1 million sq ft at end-Q1 2026, a deterministic fall of 0.4 million sq ft (2.1%). Reported supply is not a vacancy rate.

claims.headline: West End H1 prime £175.10; City year-to-May £135
claims.text: Savills reported West End average prime rent of £175.10 per sq ft for H1 2026 (January to June), up 2.3% on H1 2025, and City average achieved prime rent of £135 per sq ft for the year to May 2026. Different averaging windows are not comparable.

claims.headline: H1 Grade A: West End £106.17 vs City £76.21
claims.text: Savills reported H1 2026 average Grade A rents of £76.21 per sq ft in the City (up 7% on H1 2025) and £106.17 per sq ft in the West End. Deterministic comparison shows the West End level £29.96 per sq ft (39.3%) above the City on the same H1 period.

claims.headline: H1 2026 development starts 1.5m sq ft, one new-build
claims.text: Savills reported development starts fell sharply in H1 2026 to just 1.5 million sq ft, with only one new-build scheme breaking ground (Delta at Paddington, 234,000 sq ft, delivered by TfL and Helical) and the remaining 14 starts being refurbishments.

claims.headline: Savills forecast: 22m sq ft completions by 2029
claims.text: Savills forecasts Central London development completions reaching 22 million sq ft by end-2029 across 148 schemes with a realistic prospect of delivery. Projected completions are not current availability.

claims.headline: 1 Appold Street pre-let 268,000 sq ft at £104 per sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported the largest pre-let and transaction to complete was Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer's acquisition of British Land and GIC's 1 Appold Street, EC2 (268,000 sq ft) at £104 per sq ft for a 21-year term, published 1 May 2026.

claims.headline: City Fringe vacancy 8.2% at end-2025
claims.text: Savills reported City Fringe vacancy of 8.2% at end-Q4 2025 versus 8.3% at end-Q3 2025. City Fringe is not Midtown, and Midtown itself remains unmeasured in reviewed evidence.

claims.headline: Hammersmith 26% and VNEB 18% vacancy in Q4 2025
claims.text: Savills reported Q4 2025 vacancy of 26% in Hammersmith and 18% in VNEB, described as West End Fringe sub-markets. These are selected wider-London districts, not a wider-London average.

claims.headline: Bank Rate maintained at 3.75%
claims.text: The Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee voted by a majority of 6-3 at its meeting ending 16 September 2026 to maintain Bank Rate at 3.75%. This is a UK-wide policy rate, not a London office financing cost.

claims.headline: London resident labour rates, May-July 2026
claims.text: ONS regional labour data published 15 September 2026 report London resident rates for May to July 2026: employment 73.9% and inactivity 20.5% for residents aged 16 to 64, and unemployment 6.8% for economically active residents aged 16 and over. Residence-based, not office employment.

claims.headline: London real GVA grew 0.3% in 2023
claims.text: GLA analysis reports the most recent ONS release showed London real GVA grew by only 0.3% in 2023, compared with 0.4% for the UK as a whole. This is a historical observed release, not a current growth measurement.

claims.headline: Grade A 78% of Q1 take-up; Grade B 73% of supply
claims.text: BNP Paribas Real Estate reported Grade A space accounted for 78.0% of all Central London take-up in Q1 2026, and that Grade B was 73% of Central London office supply at Q1 end. These are shares of take-up and supply, not of stock.

claims.headline: BREEAM-rated buildings show 49% West End, 39% City rent premium
claims.text: Savills reported that in H1 2026 average rents in BREEAM 'Excellent' or 'Outstanding' buildings were 49% higher than in non-rated buildings in the West End and 39% higher in the City. A static premium does not establish a widening gap or a causal amenity effect.

claims.headline: Deutsche Bank to take YY London space from early 2028
claims.text: Deutsche Bank announced it will take space at YY London, Canary Wharf, from early 2028; the building is described as fully electric and targeting net-zero-in-operation. This is an announced future plan, not observed 2026 occupation or verified net-zero achievement.

claims.headline: 28% of GB workers hybrid in early 2025
claims.text: ONS reported that 28% of workers in Great Britain were hybrid workers between 8 January and 30 March 2025. This is Great Britain survey context, not a London office attendance measure, and it is stale relative to the briefing date.

claims.headline: Tightening competing supply supports well-specified space
claims.text: For landlords, a reported 20% year-on-year fall in Central London availability and sharply reduced H1 2026 development starts together point to tightening competing supply, which supports pricing on well-specified space.

claims.headline: Quality and certification concentrate occupier demand
claims.text: For landlords, the reported 78% Grade A share of Q1 2026 Central London take-up and the 49% West End / 39% City BREEAM rent premium indicate occupier preference is concentrated in higher-quality, certified stock, so refurbishment and certification of existing assets is the more immediate route to competing for demand than new-build delivery.

claims.headline: Watch CWG availability disclosure basis
claims.text: Watch whether Canary Wharf Group's next earnings disclosure restates the 20% year-on-year fall in Central London availability with a defined reference period and measurement basis, and whether Docklands supply remains broadly steady.

claims.headline: Watch Canary Wharf proposal and letting conversion
claims.text: Watch whether the JPMorgan 265-metre Canary Wharf tower proposal secures planning approval, and whether the LS Estates defence and AI marketing at the former Credit Suisse support office converts into a signed letting.

claims.headline: Watch starts-to-completions pipeline revision
claims.text: Watch whether Savills' next Central London release shows H1 2026's 1.5 million sq ft of development starts translating into a lower forward completions profile, and whether its stated completions forecast is revised.

claims.headline: Watch lab-to-office repositioning in Canary Wharf
claims.text: Watch whether the 17 Columbus Courtyard refit repositions away from the 60% laboratory allocation given lower-than-expected short-term life-sciences interest, and whether defence and AI occupiers take space in Canary Wharf refurbishments.
